Thought: All 33 boroughs match between datasets and adjacency is symmetric. Now I'll implement Moran's I using row-standardized weights and a permutation test with at least 500 shuffles to assess significance.
Action:
```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_second_half_2017_to_first_half_2018.csv'

crime_df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

crime_df['change'] = crime_df['first_half_2018_value'] - crime_df['second_half_2017_value']

# Build lookup from borough to index
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(crime_df['borough'])}
n = len(crime_df)

# Build adjacency matrix (binary, symmetric)
adj_matrix = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)
for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    adj_matrix[i, j] = 1

# Row-standardize weights
weights = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    row_sum = adj_matrix[i].sum()
    if row_sum > 0:
        weights[i] = adj_matrix[i] / row_sum
    else:
        weights[i] = 0  # isolated node

# Get change values in borough order
x = crime_df['change'].values
z = x - x.mean()

# Compute Moran's I
numerator = np.dot(z, np.dot(weights, z))
denominator = np.dot(z, z)
moran_i = numerator / denominator

print('Observed Moran I:', moran_i)

# Permutation test with 999 shuffles (>=500 as required)
np.random.seed(42)
perm_stats = np.empty(999)
for perm in range(999):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.dot(z_perm, np.dot(weights, z_perm))
    denom_perm = np.dot(z_perm, z_perm)
    perm_stats[perm] = num_perm / denom_perm

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(moran_i)) + 1) / (len(perm_stats) + 1)
print('Permutation p-value:', p_value)
print('Mean permuted I:', perm_stats.mean())
print('Std permuted I:', perm_stats.std())
print('Min permuted I:', perm_stats.min())
print('Max permuted I:', perm_stats.max())
```

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/changespillover/changespillover_no2crime_crime_second_half_2017_to_first_half_2018.csv'

# Load data and compute change
crime_df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj_df = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

crime_df['change'] = crime_df['first_half_2018_value'] - crime_df['second_half_2017_value']

# Drop NaNs
clean_df = crime_df.dropna(subset=['change']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Build index lookup
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(clean_df['borough'])}
n = len(clean_df)

# Build adjacency matrix and row-standardized weights
adj_clean = adj_df[adj_df['borough'].isin(clean_df['borough']) & adj_df['neighbor'].isin(clean_df['borough'])].copy()
adj_matrix = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)
for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    adj_matrix[borough_to_idx[row['borough']], borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]] = 1

row_sums = adj_matrix.sum(axis=1)
weights = np.zeros((n, n))
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        weights[i] = adj_matrix[i] / row_sums[i]

# Observed Moran's I
x = clean_df['change'].values
z = x - x.mean()
numerator = np.dot(z, np.dot(weights, z))
denominator = np.dot(z, z)
moran_i = numerator / denominator
print('Observed Moran I:', moran_i)

# Permutation test: 999 shuffles (>= 500)
np.random.seed(42)
perm_stats = np.empty(999)
for perm in range(999):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    perm_stats[perm] = np.dot(z_perm, np.dot(weights, z_perm)) / np.dot(z_perm, z_perm)

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = (np.sum(np.abs(perm_stats) >= np.abs(moran_i)) + 1) / (len(perm_stats) + 1)
print('Permutation p-value:', p_value)
print('Mean permuted I:', np.nanmean(perm_stats))
print('Std permuted I:', np.nanstd(perm_stats))
print('Min permuted I:', np.nanmin(perm_stats))
print('Max permuted I:', np.nanmax(perm_stats))
print('Perm stats contain NaN?', np.isnan(perm_stats).any())
```
